## Summary of fixes (Part (a): threshold structure & maximal-order asymptotics)

I reviewed the full proof and found two genuine, related errors in Part (a), both now fixed in solution.tex. Part (b) was already rigorous and is unchanged.

### Error 1 (incorrect recursion for the thresholds a_k)
Lemma "threshold" claimed a_k = min{n : d(n) = a_{k-1}} ( = M(a_{k-1}) ). This is FALSE at the boundary: it gives a_2 = M(2) = 2, whereas a_2 = 4 (since 2 is prime, k_d(2)=1, so 2 in A_1 not A_2). The displayed claim "least integer with t divisors for t=2,4,6,12,60 namely 4,6,12,60,5040" is internally inconsistent because M(2)=2, not 4. The real reason a_2=4 is the COMPOSITENESS requirement: A_2={n composite : d(n) prime}, min = 4 (d(4)=3). Also M is non-monotone (M(5)=16>12=M(6)), so "minimize n by taking d(n)=a_{k-1}" is not valid.

Fix: I restated the lemma with correct, fully proved facts:
- A_k = {n composite : d(n) in A_{k-1}} for k>=2 (compositeness automatic for k>=3 since a_2=4);
- (a_k) strictly increasing (n>d(n)>=a_{k-1} for n in A_k);
- correct two-sided bound g(a_k) <= a_{k+1} <= M(a_k), with M(t)=min{n:d(n)=t} and g(T)=min_{t>=T}M(t) the nondecreasing envelope (envelope needed precisely because M is non-monotone).
Values a_1..a_6 = 2,4,6,12,60,5040 are re-derived correctly (g(a_k)=M(a_k) for these small k pins them exactly).

### Error 2 (the Theta(loglog N/logloglog N) asymptotic was only half-proved)
The old Theorem proved the lower bound on K_d(N) via a_{k+1}<=M(a_k)+Wigert, but the UPPER bound on K_d(N) used only the crude descent d(n)<=n^{3/4}, giving K_d(N)=O(loglog N), strictly WEAKER than the claimed Theta(loglog N/logloglog N). The matching upper bound was missing.

Fix: Using the new lower bound a_{k+1} >= g(a_k) plus the Wigert/Ramanujan lower bound on M(t) (log g(T) = (1+o(1)) logT loglogT/log2), the recursion becomes a genuine two-sided asymptotic b_{k+1}=(1+o(1)) b_k log b_k/log2 (b_k=log a_k), so loglog a_k = (1+o(1)) k log k with both directions. I also rewrote the recursion-solving step rigorously: c_k=loglog a_k satisfies c_{k+1}=c_k+log c_k+O(1); via MVT, L_k:=c_k/log c_k satisfies L_{k+1}-L_k=1+o(1), so by Stolz L_k=(1+o(1))k, giving c_k=(1+o(1))k log k. Inversion gives K_d(N)=(1+o(1)) loglog N/logloglog N with matching bounds.

Numerically verified: k_d values and a_1..a_6; boundary a_2=4; g(a_k)=M(a_k) for k<=5; and that c_{k+1}=c_k+log c_k yields c_k/(k log k) -> 1 (very slow, ~ loglog k/log k, but monotone toward 1).

The crude uniform bound k_d(n) <= loglog n/log(4/3) + 5 is retained, now correctly described as O(loglog n) (weaker than the sharp maximal order). Summary section and all cross-references updated; no dangling references remain.

These were the substantive gaps; repaired, Part (a) is now rigorous and consistent with Part (b).
